Priya (sec-eng): Heads-up: we're moving from a flat log TTL to a split strategy to reduce blast radius. Plan: 0-21d raw events, 22-540d pseudonymized index (stable tenant salt), >540d cold encrypted blobs. Need input on RBAC for re-identification and how SOC requests should be handled.

Liam (infra): Sounds reasonable. One difference from prior designs: instead of storing the salt directly, propose per-tenant key-encrypted salt blobs. A keywrap-service holds a single role with KMS decrypt rights and only returns the salt to a short-lived worker process that performs re-id transforms. No human ever sees plaintext salt.

Nora (SOC): For incidents, SOC will need to pivot quickly. Can we support an automated approval path for high-severity incidents (pager present + incident ID) that issues a 2-hour ephemeral reveal token? Otherwise manual approval will slow triage.

Theo (forensics): Requirements from forensics: we need reproducible hashes across rotations and the ability to trace which salt epoch produced a hash. Suggest keeping a salt-index ledger (metadata only) that maps epoch IDs to key-encrypted blobs. The reveal flow must accept an epoch selector.

Priya (sec-eng): Good call. Also privacy wants a field inventory. We'll mask the obvious: email, ipv4, mac, device_id, user_id. Keep usernames truncated, not reversible. Legal: any concerns about re-id being considered "processing of personal data"?

Legal Bot: Re-identification is sensitive. We need documented lawful purpose per reveal event, recorded approver identity, and retention justification in the Legal intake. Please attach the field inventory and expected access patterns.

Liam (infra): Implementation sketch: 

```
# keywrap-service flow
1) salt_{tenant}_{epoch} encrypted with CMK logs-cmk -> stored in blobstore
2) analyst/SOC opens reveal request -> creates ticket with purpose
3) ticket service returns short-lived ticket T
4) keywrap-service verifies T + ACLs, calls KMS:Decrypt on salt blob
5) worker uses salt to run re-identify query in isolated ephemeral pod
6) results stored to secure S3 path with TTL and audit record
```

Liam (infra): IAM: keywrap-service role has kms:Decrypt on salt blobs only; no human roles get kms decrypt. CMK key policy must allow previous key versions for rotation. We'll add condition to KMS decrypt allowing only the keywrap-service principal and the CI test principal.

Nora (SOC): For the automated path: incident detection -> create ticket T with severity HIGH -> on-call lead (or rotation autopolicy) approves -> reveal token issued for 2h. We should log approver user and incident ID in the audit event. Also rate-limit reveals per incident.

Theo (forensics): Test cases we need: epoch rotation mapping, expired-token attempts, failed-decrypt fallback (should return masked results, not raw PII), and perf SLA (re-id job should start within 10 minutes of ticket approval).

deploy-bot: CI change required: index mapping for pseudonymized index and a new job that runs ephemeral re-id pods. Example config snippet: `{"indexes": {"sec_raw": {"ttl_days": 21}, "sec_pseudo": {"ttl_days": 519, "transform": "pseudonymize:tenant_salted"}}}`. Created ticket INFRA-8672 for canary.

Priya (sec-eng): RBAC proposal (draft): `forensics:reid` grants ability to request re-id; `soc:reveal` can auto-approve under incident autopolicy; `analyst:read_pseudo` can query pseudonymized index. I'll attach a matrix to the Legal ticket.

Liam (infra): Also note: we should instrument every reveal with immutable audit entries: ticket id, approver, requestor, epoch used, pod id, query hash, and TTL expiry. Store audit logs in a separate immutable ledger (write-once S3 + object-lock).

Nora (SOC): Please add a short runbook patch: how to request reveal during an active pager, who can approve, and how to escalate if a reveal fails. I'll add that to incident-runbook PR.

Theo (forensics): One more ask: ability to do limited bulk re-id for legal subpoenas with separate workflow (longer TTL, legal approver, and additional audit controls). Not to be conflated with SOC reveal.

Priya (sec-eng): action items: 1) I will post field inventory + retention rationale to Legal intake today. 2) Liam to PR keywrap-service IAM and CMK policy (due Fri). 3) deploy-bot to run a single-tenant canary in staging next week (INFRA-8672). 4) Nora to draft SOC autopolicy and runbook snippet.

Liam (infra): I'll also add a test harness that simulates key rotation and validates lookup across epochs. Tagging Theo for verification.

Theo (forensics): ack, will validate. Please tag me on the canary ticket.

Priya (sec-eng): Thanks team. Let's keep access narrow and audited; re-id is allowed only when justified and recorded. I'll follow up with the Legal ticket ref when created. :lock:
